plan.title: bug(scope): the one-PR path has no lawful worker path (write fence reads the merge base; swarm:launch needs origin; no task alias)

narratives.Description: The #6273 one-PR path has no lawful worker path: the #5656 write fence reads a brief's file_scope only from the merge base, so a one-PR brief gets an empty fence; swarm:launch refuses a brief absent from origin/<deliveryBranch>; and tasks/policy.yml has no set-one-pr-scope-proof alias. This story lets the existing one-PR mint proof (evaluateOnePrScopeProofGate plus evaluateMintLevelRecord) stand in for the merge-base read in one shared fence loader and in the swarm:launch origin probe, adds the task alias and corrects the control wording. It adds no new gate, command, approval or stop; the bound contract is successor lean comment 6906450838 on #6361, with the verified-claims table in comment 6906496136.
narratives.Overview:
1. One fence loader. Behind the existing `loadStoryWriteFence` seam, the loader returns the merge-base brief's fence when the brief exists on the merge base (unchanged). When the brief is absent there, it returns the working-tree brief's `file_scope` only if `evaluateOnePrScopeProofGate` (PROJECT-DEFINITION at the fence's own resolved merge-base SHA against the head copy) returns `mint` and `evaluateMintLevelRecord` admits the head record, intent preimage and brief. Any other result is today's empty fence. Every caller uses this one loader: `hooks/scope.ts` positive allow and the eligible partition, and the three defaults in `hooks/dispatcher.ts`.
2. No stale admission. A mint-admitted fence is not served from the memo keyed on the merge-base SHA. It is evaluated again on each call, or keyed on the digests of the head brief, record, intent preimage and PROJECT-DEFINITION. The hook path fails closed and never throws.
3. The record stays protected. The always-on protected-store deny on `.deft/approved-scope/` keeps running before story allow, so a mint-admitted `file_scope` that lists the record pair does not admit Write or Edit to those files.
4. Honest deny text. When the merge-base level is `mint` and the selected brief is absent from the merge base, the #5656 deny prints the mint reject reason and names `scope:record-approved-scope`, not promote or activate.
5. Launch from the pushed one-PR branch. When a selected brief is not a blob on `origin/<deliveryBranch>`, `swarm:launch` accepts it if it is a blob on `origin/<base-branch>` (the pushed one-PR branch passed as `--base-branch`) and the same two evaluators admit it at that ref's tip against its merge base with the delivery branch. The dest worktree is created from that ref. No brief or record bytes are copied. Finalize and fresh-clone rules of #4714 are unchanged.
6. Task alias. `tasks/policy.yml` gains `set-one-pr-scope-proof`, in the same shape as `set-spec-guard-enforcement`.
7. Control wording. `MINT_LEVEL_LOCAL_CONTROL_LINE` and `content/docs/scope-provenance.md` name the control without a human merge as the local mint gate plus the protected-store deny on `.deft/approved-scope/`, and say that the shell-write residual (#3597, #3595) also reaches local scope admission.
narratives.Constraint:
- Calling the whole provenance evaluator from the per-write hook, or a second copy of the admit checks (comment 6906425592 finding 1).
- Copying the brief or the record from the operator's working tree into the dest (comments 6906390344 finding 1 and 6906425592 finding 3).
- A new approval, signature or human stop for the worker path. The signed level stays on #5862.
- Reading the working-tree brief whenever `DEFT_ACTIVE_SCOPE` is set, with the mint optional.
- Admitting a head brief that widens a brief already on the merge base. That stays with #4956.
narratives.UserStory: As a worker on a one-PR story, I want the write fence and swarm:launch to accept a brief covered by a valid one-PR mint, so that the story ships in one PR without a hand-applied patch or a separate activation PR.
narratives.ImplementationPlan:
1. packages/core/src/policy/write-fence.ts: behind the loadStoryWriteFence seam, keep the merge-base fence when the brief exists on the merge base; when it is absent, return the working-tree file_scope only when evaluateOnePrScopeProofGate (PROJECT-DEFINITION at the fence's resolved merge-base SHA against the head copy) returns mint and evaluateMintLevelRecord admits the head record, intent preimage and brief; otherwise return the empty fence. Do not serve a mint-admitted fence from the merge-base-SHA memo (evaluate per call, or key on the head brief, record, intent preimage and PROJECT-DEFINITION digests). Fail closed; never throw on the hook path.
2. packages/core/src/hooks/dispatcher.ts and packages/core/src/hooks/scope.ts: route the scope.ts positive allow and eligible partition and the three dispatcher defaults through that one loader. Keep the always-on protected-store deny on .deft/approved-scope/ before story allow. When the merge-base level is mint and the brief is absent there, the #5656 deny prints the mint reject reason and names scope:record-approved-scope, not promote or activate.
3. packages/core/src/swarm/origin-active-brief.ts and packages/core/src/swarm/launch.ts: when a brief is not a blob on origin/<deliveryBranch>, accept it if it is a blob on origin/<base-branch> and the same two evaluators admit it at that tip against its merge base with the delivery branch; create the dest worktree from that ref; copy no brief or record bytes. The #4714 finalize and fresh-clone rules stay unchanged.
4. tasks/policy.yml: add set-one-pr-scope-proof in the same engine:invoke shape as set-spec-guard-enforcement.
5. packages/core/src/policy/one-pr-scope-proof.ts (MINT_LEVEL_LOCAL_CONTROL_LINE) and content/docs/scope-provenance.md: name the no-human-merge control as the local mint gate plus the protected-store deny on .deft/approved-scope/, and state that the shell-write residual (#3597, #3595) also reaches local scope admission.
6. Tests as evidence for every clause: write-fence.test.ts, dispatcher-write-gate.test.ts, dispatcher-spawn-dest.test.ts, dispatcher-active-scope.test.ts, scope.test.ts, one-pr-scope-proof.test.ts, origin-active-brief.test.ts, launch.test.ts and a new taskfile_policy_one_pr_alias.test.ts; run the swarm verify_commands. One CHANGELOG.md [Unreleased] line.
7. packages/core/src/scope-provenance/known-machine.ts: write-fence.ts now imports one-pr-scope-proof.ts, which closes the cycle acceptance-evidence -> acceptance-resolver -> hooks/scope -> write-fence -> one-pr-scope-proof -> compare-intent/extract-intent -> known-machine; ITEM_MACHINE_KEYS reads ACCEPTANCE_EVIDENCE_KEY at module top level, so it throws a TDZ ReferenceError when extract-intent loads first. Use the literal key there to break the init-order dependence. The widen lands with a same-PR one-PR mint (#6273), so file_scope also lists the record pair.
Rejects (Constraint): no call of the whole provenance evaluator from the per-write hook and no second copy of the admit checks; no brief or record copy into the dest; no new approval, signature or human stop; no working-tree read on DEFT_ACTIVE_SCOPE alone; no head brief that widens a merge-base brief (#4956).

## In plain English
The one-PR path lets a maintainer land a new brief and its code in one pull request. CI accepts it through a human-presence mint record carried in the same PR. But the worker that must write the code is stopped earlier. The local write fence reads the brief's allowed paths from the merge base, and a one-PR brief is not there by design. The fence's own recovery advice (promote, activate) rewrites the brief and voids the mint. `swarm:launch` also refuses, because it wants the brief on the delivery branch. The issue proposes that both places accept the proof CI already accepts, with no new check. The open question is whether that proof is safe to reuse locally: the mint is a file, the fence exists to stop an agent from widening its own scope, and the one-PR code names the fence as the control for the mint.

## Pains

## In plain English

Problem: the one-PR path lets a maintainer land a new brief, its human mint record and its code in one pull request, but the worker that writes the code was stopped before CI. The local write fence read the brief's allowed paths only from the merge base, where a one-PR brief does not exist, and its recovery advice voided the mint. `swarm:launch` refused the brief for the same reason, and the task alias for the policy setter was missing.

Accepted solution: when a brief is absent from the merge base, the write fence admits the working-tree brief's allowed paths only if the merge base turns the one-PR level on and the mint record matches that exact brief. It uses the two functions CI already uses, in one loader shared by every reader of the fence, and never serves a cached answer for a changed brief. Writes to the mint record stay refused by the separate always-on rule that runs before the brief's paths are looked at. `swarm:launch` accepts such a brief from the pushed one-PR branch and builds the worker's checkout from that branch. The task alias is added. The control wording is corrected.

The design adds no new gate, command, approval or stop. One limit is stated and accepted: a mint record written by a shell command that the classifier misses (#3597, #3595) would now also open the local fence for that brief. No leftover next-build.

## Summary

The #6273 one-PR path (mint level, `onePrScopeProof: mint`, no human merge since #6354) has no lawful way for a worker to do the product work. Found on its first real use (#6327, wave 2a, 2026-11-15).

## What we saw

1. **Write fence reads the merge base.** The #5656 Write/Edit fence reads `file_scope` from the merge base (origin/master). A one-PR brief is not on origin/master by design, so every product edit is refused, even with `DEFT_ACTIVE_SCOPE` naming the local running brief. The fence's recovery (promote / activate) changes the brief and voids the mint. The #6327 worker ended up writing a patch outside the repo for the operator to apply.
2. **No in-session launch.** `swarm:launch` needs the brief active on origin/master (#4714), which the one-PR path skips by design.
3. **No task alias.** `policy:set-one-pr-scope-proof` shipped as a `deft` verb with no `tasks/policy.yml` alias, so `task policy:set-one-pr-scope-proof` fails in this repo. The operator script stopped half-applied and the resume called the core setter.

## Expected

A one-PR story runs like any other story, without a second PR:

- The write fence admits a one-PR brief's `file_scope` when the brief is running on the branch and the one-PR mint covers it (the same proof `verify:scope-provenance` uses through `resolveOnePrGate`).
- `swarm:launch` accepts a one-PR brief on the same proof instead of requiring it on origin/master.
- `task policy:set-one-pr-scope-proof` works in this repo.

No new check: this lets the existing mint stand in for the merge-base read.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a running one-PR brief covered by a valid mint, when a worker edits a path inside its `file_scope`, then the write fence admits the edit.
- Given the same brief, when an edit targets a path outside its `file_scope`, then the fence still refuses.
- Given a running one-PR brief covered by a valid mint and absent from origin/master, when `swarm:launch` runs for it, then the launch proceeds.
- `task policy:set-one-pr-scope-proof` runs the `deft` verb in this repo.

Refs #6273. Refs #6354. Refs #6327. Related: #5656, #4714.
